data.name: Chitraksh
data.gender_notes: Chitraksh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Chitraksh is a name for Varaha Avatar of Lord Vishnu, who has a thousand eyes. This form of Vishnu is revered for his all-seeing and protective nature. The name Chitraksh carries the meaning “God with the thousand eyes” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chitraksh usually hope their child will grow to embody god with the thousand eyes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chitraksh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God with the thousand eyes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chitraksh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chitraksh holds a significant place in Hindu culture as it is associated with one of the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu - Varaha Avatar. Chitraksh is also known as the thousand-eyed form of Vishnu. This form embodies Lord Vishnu's omnipresent and omniscient nature, inspiring awe and reverence in the hearts of devotees. Its representation in art, literature, and religious texts provides an essential part of Hindu heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Chitraksh is a symbol of divine protection, wisdom, and consciousness expansion. The thousand eyes of Lord Varaha represent Lord Vishnu's infinite knowledge and awareness of the universe. As a spiritual concept, the name Chitraksh inspires deeper contemplation and devotion towards divine intelligence and the underlying interconnectedness of all beings. It serves as a reminder of the infinite, omniscient nature of the divine, encouraging seekers on their spiritual journey toward self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chitraksh: The radiant one with the divine, all-seeing gaze. Symbolizing wisdom, insight, and protection from inner and outer adversities.

historical_references.reference: Chitraketu was a famous king in ancient India, who ruled over the Videha kingdom in the Kosala region around 6th century BCE. He was a pious and just ruler, known for his generosity and wisdom. The name 'Chitraketu' is derived from 'Chitra' meaning 'painted' and 'Ketu' meaning 'moon'. The name signifies the 'painted moon' and is also symbolic of the king's radiance and power.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Videha kingdom, Kosala region

historical_references.reference: Chitraseni was the name of a famous sage or Rishi in Hindu mythology. He is believed to have lived around the 8th century BCE and was a celebrated poet and scholar. The name 'Chitraseni' is derived from 'Chitra' meaning 'painted' and 'Seni' meaning 'head'. This name is symbolic of Chitraseni's brilliance and wisdom, and he is also known as the 'painted sage'.
